title: Define request-fidelity SLIs per endpoint with session-aware eviction and quorum-based regional failover policy
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a concrete SLI/SLO specification for 'request-fidelity' per model endpoint that captures both latency and end-to-end fidelity (non-functional correctness) with special handling for session/tenant-aware KV cache effects. Define error budget burn rules, circuit-breaker thresholds, and a quorum-based regional failover policy that coordinates rollback/fallback when error budgets are exceeded across regions. Deliverables: canonical SLI definitions, SLO targets for tiered routes, policy for progressive load shedding, and an operational runbook for cross-region failover involving quorum checks and graceful KV cache invalidation.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical 'request-fidelity' SLI is published that includes: latency (p50/p95/p99), per-request quality classification (match/noise/regression), and token-level failure modes
SLO targets defined per-tier (critical/standard/dev) with numeric thresholds and expected error-budget burn rates
A documented algorithm for attributing fidelity degradations to KV cache miss/eviction vs model variant quality and weighting those in error-budget burn
Circuit-breaker thresholds and hysteresis defined (short-window burn + long-window burn + tail-latency constraints) and validated in the staging replay harness
Quorum-based regional failover policy documented with decision matrix: when to failover, partial failover (subset of tenants), and KV cache invalidation plan to avoid stale responses
Runbook with playbook entries for on-call: detection alerts, manual override steps, and automated rollback safeguards

design_decisions: Use a composite SLI 'request-fidelity' combining latency quantiles and a binary fidelity classifier rather than separate 'quality' and 'latency' SLIs to simplify runbook decisions.

Attribute fidelity regressions to KV-cache misses by emitting 'fidelity_attribution' signals at inference time (cache_hit=true/false + classifier outcome); use a weighted burn algorithm where cache-miss-caused failures count as 0.7 of a full failure for error budget purposes.
Adopt quorum-based regional failover: require majority of configured regions to be degraded before global failover; allow per-tenant partial failover when tenant is pinned to a region.
Circuit breakers will consider instantaneous burn (5m), medium burn (1h), and tail-latency spike (p99) together; rule: if two of three exceed thresholds, open circuit for affected model variant.
KV cache invalidation during failover will be staged: invalidate local TTL, then global, to avoid mass stale-responses and cold-start storms; include warm-up policy for baseline capacity
